name: Makuri Naga
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

tone_statements.citation: Shi, Vong Tsuh. 2009. Discourse studies of Makuri Naga narratives. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xiii+168 pp.
tone_statements.quote: This language seems to have three phonemic tones in both open and closed syllables. They are low, falling, and high. … 1) Low [kʰā ] (to) keep [pɔ̄ŋ ] threshing place 2) Falling [kʰâ ] crate [pɔ̂ŋ ] cup 3) High [kʰá ] (to) tend [pɔ́ŋ ] (to) bloom Table 5: Phonemic tones Syllables closed with [ʔ] never occur with high tone. They can appear with either low or falling tone, e.g. /kʰāʔ/ ‘one’ and /kʰâʔ/ ‘to rake with hands/ with implements’. Since the orthography of the language does not mark tones, the present data will not mark them either.
tone_statements.summary: Three phonemic tones, low, falling and high, on open and closed syllables; glottal-stop-final syllables take only low or falling. Orthography and texts do not mark tone. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Lubbe, Melissa, Tiffany Priest & Sigrid Lew. 2022. A preliminary phonology and Latin-based orthography of Para Naga (Jejara), Northwest Myanmar. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 15(2).
sources.note: Sister language (Para Naga) in the same Payap/SIL Myanmar Naga project; may contain comparative notes on Makuri prosody and cites the survey literature; open access on eVols but download could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2026. Patkaian (Northern Naga). Oxford handbook chapter (Zenodo 22253033).
sources.note: Mentions Makuri once, only as a contact source for Paung Nyuan ('the number one khat', line 1087); nothing on Makuri phonology or stress.
No phonology at all; only classification, dialects (Shi 2009:5 lists Phuvle, Makheotle, Sengphuvle, Muvle, Jeile) and bibliography (Shi 2009; Shintani 2018; LSDO 2006; Saul 2005; Hsiu 2021).
